text: Databases are essential tools for storing and organizing information. The most common type is the relational database, which uses tables made up of rows and columns. You interact with these databases using SQL (Structured Query Language) to run queries, which retrieve or update specific data. Before building a database, you need data modeling—planning how tables relate to each other to avoid duplication. Indexes are also crucial because they speed up searches, like a book's index. However, not all data fits neatly into tables. NoSQL databases, such as document stores or key-value systems, handle unstructured or rapidly changing data more flexibly. Choosing between SQL and NoSQL depends on your project’s needs: SQL for complex relationships, NoSQL for scalability and flexibility.
